Idiosyncratic single-name upside is real and can dominate the cumulative record (CRM +39.10%) -- the mirror image of single-name downside (AMZN/PCG). It is NOT a repeatable strategy edge; treat both fat tails as luck-of-the-draw. The lasting lesson is symmetric: MA-20/60 trend entries carry fat single-name tails in BOTH directions -- size discipline is the only defense. Last week made the two-sided point cleanly: Bull led on Tuesday's down tape, LAGGED Thursday's strong up tape, and gave back MORE than SPY on Friday's tech-led pullback because its biggest winners are the high-beta names that led lower.
avoid: Extended entries (price well above EMA-20 at entry) -- CONFIRMED LOSER, thesis RESOLVED by AMZN (entered Aug 4 at +15.2% above EMA20, stopped -6.57% Aug 17) and META (Jul 15 ~8.5% ext, stopped -8.04% Jul 23). Surviving extended admits are fine now (MSFT +2.91%, QQQ still RED -1.26%/3.06% cushion, CRM the +39% exception) but that does not vindicate the entry. Firm rule stands: treat >~6-8% above-EMA extension as size-DOWN or wait-for-pullback; when it co-occurs with a shallow cross, SKIP. MSTR correctly SKIPPED 9/1 on +17.2% extension among three stacked flags.

STACKED-FLAG entries (shallow cross + extended above EMA + thin liquidity together) -- SKIP, not size-down: PDBC (0.15% cross + ~6% ext + thin liq, Jul 24) stopped -2.40%. One flag -> size down; two or more stacked -> skip. Applied correctly repeatedly: SLV skipped Aug 28 (two flags), MSTR skipped Sep 1 (three flags), EWZ skipped Sep 2 (0.033% noise cross + 7.05% ext). HAL 9/4 was a legitimate size-down (two SOFT flags: 0.298% cross + 657k borderline liq, NOT extended at 5.69%) -- the boundary case, watch its follow-through.

Noise-level / opening-bar-artifact crosses -- EQT skipped Aug 28: completed-bar EMA20/60 spread only 0.0145%, far below the 0.1% shallow-cross floor; a live 0.19% read was a 917-share opening-bar artifact on a partial daily bar.
